name: Cocody Deux Plateaux
tagline: Leafy expat district with the best cafes and wifi
description: Wide tree-lined avenues of walled villas and low apartment blocks, punctuated by patisseries, sushi bars and the Vallon business strip. Embassies, international schools and Ivorian professionals fill it. Remote workers base here for generator-backed apartments, fibre internet and a supermarket on almost every corner.
bestFor: Nomads who want reliable power, fast internet and a quiet villa street to work from
pros: Most reliable fibre and backup power in the city
Dense cluster of cafes, gyms and supermarkets
Feels safe to walk in the evening
cons: Rents are among the highest in Abidjan
You need a taxi or car for almost everything
Vallon traffic backs up badly at rush hour

name: Plateau
tagline: The glass tower business core, walkable and central
description: Abidjan's compact downtown of banking towers, ministries and the pyramid-shaped Cathedrale Saint Paul, wedged between the lagoon and the Boulevard de la Republique. Office workers pack the lunch spots by day. Serviced apartments here put you within walking distance of banks, coworking and lagoon boat taxis.
bestFor: Short-stay workers who want to walk to meetings, banks and admin offices
pros: Best transport links including lagoon boat taxis
Serviced apartments and hotels with backup generators
cons: Almost dead and shuttered after office hours and on Sundays
Heavy daytime traffic and constant horn noise
Street hustling around the main boulevards

name: Marcory Zone 4
tagline: Nightlife and restaurants, the social base
description: A grid of low-rise blocks south of the lagoon where Rue Paul Langevin and Rue des Jardins line up bars, Lebanese bakeries, Vietnamese kitchens and late-night maquis. It draws consultants, contractors and a young international crowd. Furnished one-bed rentals are common and the airport is fifteen minutes away.
bestFor: Sociable nomads who want restaurants and bars within walking distance of the flat
pros: Best eating and drinking density in the city
Close to the airport and the port
cons: Bar noise carries late into the night on weekends
Petty theft happens on the darker side streets
Bridge traffic to Plateau is a slog at peak times

name: Riviera Golf
tagline: Quiet lagoon-side apartments near the third bridge
description: A newer stretch of Cocody along the lagoon, built around the golf course with mid-rise residences, gated compounds and a handful of malls. It is calmer and greener than Deux Plateaux, popular with families and long-stay expats. The third bridge makes the run to Marcory and the airport quick.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads who value a calm apartment and space over walkable nightlife
pros: Modern apartment stock with lifts and parking
Lagoon views and noticeably cleaner air
Fast third bridge access to the south of the city
cons: Very little you can reach on foot
Nightlife means a taxi ride to Zone 4
Some streets flood hard in the rainy season

name: Treichville
tagline: Cheap, loud and the most local place to stay
description: A dense grid of numbered avenues just over the Houphouet-Boigny bridge, home to the huge covered market, the Palais de la Culture and rows of street kitchens. Rents are a fraction of Cocody. Budget nomads who want daily Ivorian life rather than an expat bubble base here.
bestFor: Budget travellers comfortable in a busy working-class quarter who want the lowest rents
pros: Cheapest rents and street food anywhere central
Walking distance to Plateau over the bridge
Constant markets, music and street life
cons: Noisy from early morning until late
Power cuts and patchy internet are common
Watch your phone at night around the market and station
